faq: Can this really fit in seven days?
We scope honestly for the time. The Premium package sets up the account structure and a headless starter. A full custom headless storefront is larger, and we quote that separately if you need it.
Do I need a BigCommerce Enterprise plan?
Some features, like multiple storefronts, depend on your plan. We check what your plan allows before we start and tell you if an upgrade is needed. Plan fees are billed by BigCommerce.
Can you connect an ERP or PIM?
We can plan the connection and set up the catalog fields it needs. Building a full ERP link is a separate integration job, which we can quote after we see your systems.
What do you need from me?
Admin access, a list of storefronts and buyer types, and any current price lists. A short call at the start helps us match the setup to your sales process.

desc:
BigCommerce multi-storefront and B2B setup lets one account serve several storefronts and wholesale buyers. Ecom Swift LLC plans the structure on paper first, then configures channels, customer groups, price lists and buying rules in your own account.

## What is a BigCommerce multi-storefront and B2B setup?

It is a way of running more than one selling surface from a single BigCommerce account. Each storefront can have its own look, domain and audience, while sharing one catalog, one order view and one admin. Alongside that, a B2B setup adds the rules wholesale buyers expect: their own prices, minimum orders, quote requests and tax-exempt status.

If you sell to consumers and trade customers, or to several regions or brands, this structure keeps things in one place instead of several separate stores.

## Why structure matters before you build

Growth often arrives in patches. A second brand gets its own store. A wholesale customer gets a discount code. Soon the same product is edited in three places and nobody trusts the stock count. Fixing that later means moving data, rewriting rules and retraining staff.

Planning the structure first is cheaper. You decide which products are shared, which prices differ by buyer, who can see what, and how orders reach your team. Then the setup follows the plan instead of working around it.

## How the setup affects revenue and workload

For wholesale buyers, the benefit is speed. A trade customer who sees their own prices, can request a quote and is not charged tax they are exempt from will reorder without phoning your sales team. That frees your staff and makes repeat orders easier.

For multiple storefronts, the benefit is focus. A separate storefront can speak to one audience, with its own navigation and promotions, while the catalog stays in sync. Staff spend time on selling instead of duplicating data. The size of the effect depends on your market and your buyers, so we describe the mechanism, not a promised outcome.

## What a strong enterprise setup includes

- A written account structure plan agreed before any configuration.
- Extra storefronts or channels, each with its own theme and domain settings.
- Shared product data, so edits flow to every storefront that carries the item.
- Customer groups for each buyer type, such as retail and trade.
- Group-based price lists that apply automatically after login.
- A quote request form and minimum order rules for wholesale buying.
- Tax-exempt customer handling.
- Staff roles and permissions, so each person sees only what they need.
- A headless starter project that reads your catalog, for teams that want a custom front end.
- Written notes and a handover call for your team.

## How we work

We start with questions: who buys from you, how they are priced, which products appear where, and who manages orders. We draw the structure and send it for approval. Only then do we configure anything.

The Basic package provides the plan and a base setup for one extra storefront or a simple B2B arrangement. Standard adds multiple storefronts, price lists, quote forms, minimum orders, tax rules and staff roles. Premium adds full B2B rules, shared catalog data and a headless starter project, with a handover call and a written guide. Where an ERP or PIM is involved, we scope that link with you rather than assume it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- List every buyer type and how each should be priced.
- Decide which products must appear on every storefront and which only on one.
- Give staff the lowest permissions that let them do their jobs.
- Test with a sample wholesale account before inviting real buyers.
- Keep the written plan, so future changes follow the same logic.

**Avoid:**
- Building separate stores when channels would share the catalog.
- Creating a different price rule for every individual customer.
- Opening a headless build without a clear reason for it.
- Giving all staff full admin rights.
- Skipping a test of tax-exempt orders.

## Who this is for

This service suits a brand adding a wholesale side to a consumer store, a company with two or more brands that want separate storefronts and one back office, and a team weighing a headless front end that wants a scoped, working starter before committing further.

## What we need from you

A description of your buyer types, your price structure and your product range, plus any price sheets you already use. We never need your password. Access is given as a staff user with the permissions the work requires. Your BigCommerce plan determines which features are available, so we check that with you early, before planning around something your account does not offer.
